question: For a routine compliance audit under Section 10.1, how often may an audit be conducted, and how much advance notice is required?
gold_answer: A routine compliance audit may be conducted no more than once in any consecutive 12-month period, and Provider must give at least 30 days' prior written notice. The audit must also take place during Licensee's normal business hours and minimize disruption.
agreement_text: §10.1 During the Term, Provider may audit Licensee's records reasonably necessary to verify compliance with the usage restrictions in this Agreement. A routine compliance audit shall be conducted only in accordance with the Operational Assurance Standard in Appendix A, which is incorporated into and forms part of this Agreement. Appendix A — Operational Assurance Standard. §A.1 Provider may conduct no more than one routine compliance audit in any consecutive 12-month period. Provider shall give Licensee at least 30 days' prior written notice. Audits shall take place during Licensee's normal business hours and shall be conducted in a manner designed to minimize disruption to Licensee's operations.

question: After termination, may Licensee retain encrypted system backups, and if so, for how long and subject to what access and use limits?
gold_answer: Yes. Licensee may retain a Residual Backup until it is overwritten in the ordinary backup cycle, but no copy may be kept for more than 90 days after termination. Access is limited to personnel responsible for disaster recovery, restoration is permitted only to address a system failure, and the backup remains subject to Section 8.1's safeguards and need-to-know restriction.
agreement_text: §1.9 Residual Backup means an encrypted copy created automatically by Licensee's systems as part of a routine backup process, rather than a copy maintained for ordinary business access. §8.1 Each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using reasonable safeguards and shall restrict access to personnel who need it to perform their duties under this Agreement. §11.3 Upon termination, Licensee shall cease using the Service Materials and delete them in accordance with the applicable deletion procedures, except as permitted under Section 11.5. §11.5 Despite Section 11.3, Licensee may retain Residual Backups until they are overwritten in the ordinary backup cycle, provided that no copy is retained for more than 90 days after termination. A Residual Backup may be accessed only by personnel responsible for disaster recovery, may be restored only to address a system failure, and remains subject to Section 8.1.

question: A company has come under Licensee's common control after an acquisition but is not named in an Order Form. Does it automatically receive access rights under the license?
gold_answer: No. The company may qualify as an Affiliate under Section 1.2 because it is under common control with Licensee, but that status alone does not grant access. Sections 2.1 and 2.2 require it to be identified as an authorized affiliate in an active Order Form and to execute a joinder before it may access the Licensed Materials.
agreement_text: §1.2 Affiliate means an entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party. Control means ownership of more than 50 percent of the voting interests or the power to direct the entity's management and policies. §2.1 Subject to Section 2.2, Provider grants Licensee a non-exclusive, non-transferable right during the Term to permit its Authorized Users and those of its Affiliates specifically identified in an Order Form to access and use the Licensed Materials for Licensee's internal business purposes. §2.2 An Affiliate may access the Licensed Materials only after it has been added as an authorized affiliate to an active Order Form and has executed a joinder agreeing to be bound by the applicable terms of this Agreement. Licensee remains responsible for its Affiliates' compliance with this Agreement.

The grant in Section 2.1 is limited to Affiliates specifically identified in an Order Form, and Section 2.2 adds the requirements of an active Order Form entry and an executed joinder.
